recipes.name: Baked Mushroom Thighs
ingredients_raw: 1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of mushroom soup

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Pour the soup into a medium bowl. Fill the empty can with milk, and add to the bowl along with the parsley and onion powder. Mix well. Place bread crumbs in a shallow dish or bowl; dip chicken thighs in soup mixture, then in crumbs, and place coated pieces in a lightly greased 9x13 inch baking dish.
Drizzle with melted butter and bake in preheated oven until chicken is nicely browned and cooked through (juices run clear), about 45 minutes.

Meanwhile, place remaining soup mixture in a small saucepan and whisk in cornstarch. Cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until mixture comes to a boil; reduce heat and simmer for a minute or two until sauce thickens. Use this as a sauce when chicken is done.

raw_recipe.headline: Baked Mushroom Thighs
raw_recipe.description: Chicken thighs are dipped in a creamy mushroom mixture and bread crumbs, then baked until nicely browned.

review.reviewBody: This chicken was delicious! The golden brown crust was crunchy and sealed the juices into the chicken. I prepared this using 10 chicken legs, which I first seasoned with Fiesta brand Chicken Rub (available in Texas). Because of cross-contamination concerns with the raw chicken, I changed the method of preparation. In a shallow bowl, I mixed the 1 cup of dry bread crumbs, the ½ tsp of onion powder, and the 1 tsp of dried parsley. In a separate bowl, I added ½ can of the mushroom soup only. I rolled my seasoned chicken into the mushroom soup then rolled into the dry crumb mix. This allowed the crumb mixture to adhere to the chicken resulting in a delicious crust. I drizzled with the 2 TBLs of melted butter, and baked as instructed. I used the other ½ can of the mushroom soup and a ½ can of milk to make gravy, which we served over white rice. My husband loved this meal! Thank you Doris!

This was great. I had a little trouble getting a nice brown using panko breadcrumbs. I might try something finer on the next go-round. Also used cream instead of milk for reconstituting the soup, it didn't need any cornstarch. Added some fresh chunked and sautéed baby bellas to the sauce, and served it up with fresh sautéed spinach and little rice. Seriously GREAT meal!

Made this recipe pretty much according to directions. I added some garlic powder and pepper and increased the cornstarch to 1 1/2 tsp. The chicken came out crisp except for the bottom which was pasty. But the big disappointment was the sauce.. It was bland, flavorless and was not a good flavor match for the coating. It definitely needed some salt to begin with. I believe this would be much better tasting with Cream of Chicken soup used as a base for the sauce. The bottom of the thighs did not come out crispy. It was gummy or pasty under there. It might improve the bottom crust if these were cooked on a rack elevating from the bottom of the pan. Another option would be to avoid coating the bottom at all. I used boneless, skinless thighs and placed them in the pan flattened as opposed to rolled up. They were more than done in the suggested 45 minutes - approaching 200°. But they were still fairly moist and tender. If you use Panko crumbs, even the seasoned ones, you might want to spice it up a bit with some salt, pepper, Italian seasoning, garlic powder and Parmesan cheese. Even the seasoned variety of Panko crumbs are pretty much tasteless. To avoid any potential for cross contamination, I set aside some of the soup/milk mix to use as sauce and used the rest for dipping the raw thighs. I added another 1/2 tsp. of cornstarch to the sauce because it seemed too thin.

The thighs turned out great. Will definitely make this again. Chicken was juicy. I removed the chicken skin first and baked on a rack. I slice three mushrooms and added to the sauce. Served with ginger butter green beans, garlic spinach stuffed tomato’s, and mashed potatoes.

I made this delicious recipe tonight. The only thing I changed was that I added some sour cream to the mushroom soup coating, paprika to the bread crumbs,fresh mushrooms to the gravy and removed the skin from the thighs. The family absolutely loved it. Served with spinach sautéed in garlic, mash potatoes and a side salad. The family ate every bite. Thank you for the recipe!

Such a great recipe. My whole family loved it. My 9 year old son who never asks for seconds asked for seconds! Few changes: I used bone in but took the skin off the thighs andit made the crumbs hold together very nicely. For an extra crunchy (messy) coating dip in soup mix, crumbs, and repeat. I didn't use the butter to coat but it wasn't missing because I added it to the gravy mix along with a can of mushrooms, more parsley, and garlic powder. Mine stayed in about 50 minutes just to be sure and they were so tender. Yum! Yum! Yum! Forever in the favorites! Thank u

I used cream of mushroom with garlic (split the mixture as most suggested) and added pepper, minced onion, and garlic powder to the 'sauce', which I thickened with flour. For the chicken, I used organic BLSL breast meat which I coated in an unseasoned version of the soup mixture, then rolled in panko/onion soup mix, baked on a rack at 400 for 30 minutes and it was delicious! Served with the sauce over rice and it was a hit!

Amazing recipe! I only gave it four stars because I made some changes suggested by other reviews. I used seasoned bread crumbs and added about half a packet of onion seasoning mix. I only used about a quarter of the soup and milk mixture for dredging, the rest for the sauce. I also baked the chicken on a rack over a baking sheet, and that helped the chicken stay extra crispy, especially on the bottom. Served it over rice with the sauce and steamed broccoli. Delicious!

Only thing I was concerned about was the raw meat dipped in sauce then crumbs and then that same remainder of mix heated up for a sauce. What about contamination from raw chicken I liquid perhaps recipe shud have two bowls of soup mixture one gor dipping one for sauce... I didn't now I am thinking i should have

This was really good! I used gluten free panko crumbs but one cup only covered three thighs and that was all I had. I improvised and used crackers with fried onions for the other thighs for my non gluten free husband to eat. I had to broil on high for about 3 minutes at the end to get it to crisp up. we served with squash and white rice. I would make this again!

Everyone enjoyed this dish and I will definitely make it again. I separated the soup mix into two separate containers as suggested by others. I also added a dollup of sour cream, some grated parmesan and some freeze dried chives to the soup mix. Maybe it was just me but it didn't work for me to dip the thighs in the soup mix and roll in bread crumbs. After one dip, the crumbs were clumped together and stuck to the plate. It worked better for me to dip the chicken with my left hand and then shake bread crumbs to cover over a plate with my right. I used both thighs with bone and skin and some boneless skinless. We decided that we prefer the boneless skinless though both were delicious.
I liked how easy it was to make and the taste was okay. It just needs a little kick to spice it up.
My second time around!!! So easy and delicious!!! I’m adding fresh spinach along with it this time! I also always add fresh mushrooms as well!

This was absolutely delicious. Seasoned thighs with salt, pepper and poultry seasoning before dunking in soup. Otherwise followed recipe as written. Served with rice and sautéed asparagus. Big hit with the hubby!
Delicious! Made as directed with some garlic powder in the breadcrumbs and sauce. I did reserve half the soup mixture for serving.
I pressure cooked the chicken first, then followed the directions. We were very pleased with y
Great, even without extra sauce. Added dried onion soup mix to the breadcrumbs as recommended by a few other reviewers.

I made it last week and we loved it so much I am making it again tonight. I used Italian bread crumbs for a little bit more seasoning but other than that I made it as written and I’ll be making it again and again. Thanks for sharing. 

Brenda Whitaker-Kroth

Man, I'm disappointed to say this was kinda bland. The only thing I did differently was use boneless skinless chicken thighs. I had high hopes since I like all of the ingredients in the recipe...but it was lacking depth of flavor. Honestly though, it's not surprising since cream of anything soup is just salt lol (I still like it though!). Thanks for sharing!
My husband said this was a definite keeper. This recipe is easy, quick and good enough to serve company. I will be making this again.
